title: Generic open-image finiteness over an integral Noetherian base
statement: Let $S$ be an integral Noetherian scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme], where Noetherian means quasi-compact and locally the spectrum of a Noetherian ring. Let $\ell$ be a prime invertible in every local ring of $S$ and put $A=\mathbf F_\ell$. Let $T\to S$ be separated of finite type [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], let $j:V\hookrightarrow T$ be an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion], and let $F$ be a constructible sheaf of modules over the constant sheaf $A_V$ on the ordinary small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf, def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. There exist a nonempty open subscheme $S^\circ\subseteq S$ and $b\geq0$ such that, writing $j^\circ:V\times_SS^\circ\hookrightarrow T\times_SS^\circ$ and $F^\circ$ for the inverse image of $F$ [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], every $R^qj^\circ_*F^\circ$ is constructible and $R^qj^\circ_*F^\circ=0$ for $q>b$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. No finite-type-over-a-field, regularity, or excellence hypothesis on $S$ is imposed.

source.place: Expose XIII, Theorem 2.3.1, proof of (i), printed p.197, first sentence: generic constructibility gives a dense open of the base where constructibility and eventual vanishing hold. This is the generic finiteness input used there; the statement isolates its open-immersion, prime-field version over an integral Noetherian base, before the low-dimensional local reduction.
